newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian newspaper editor wounded in shooting.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian newspaper editor wounded in shooting.

text.p: The young editor of a Phnom Penh newspaper was shot in the stomach by an unidentified gunman late on Thursday in an attack suspected of being politically motivated, colleagues and analysts said.
Leng Samnang was in a stable condition after early morning surgery, police said on Friday.
The attack on the 26-year-old editor comes after reports of threats to several newspapers and the unsolved murders of three journalists in the past two years.
Publisher Cheng Sokna, 32, said the attack followed months of intimidation and threats and seemed to suggest it had been politically motivated.
"Frankly speaking, I criticised the CPP directly," he said in reference to his newspaper's stance on co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.

Political observers said the shooting was seen as a reflection of political tensions between Hun Sen and co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.

"Violence against journalists tends to arise out of political conflicts," said one political analyst. "There's a direct relationship between tensions between political parties and violence against journalists associated with those political parties."

A December 31 issue of the Idea of Cambodia's Children newspaper, seen on newstands in Phnom Penh on Friday, carried headlines such as, "Vietnamese in Cambodia keep Hun Sen in power", "No communist regime gives justice to the people", and an article suggesting that CPP General Keo Pong be imprisoned.
Local journalists said the paper is aligned with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party.

A senior CPP official strongly denied the reports of intimidation. "The CPP members and party never intimidate journalists. We have never intimidated anyone," said the official, who declined to be named.

Police at the hospital where Leng Samnang, who has a wife and three children, underwent three hours of surgery early on Friday said they could not yet conclude the motivation for the attack or the identity of the assailants.
Cheng Sokna said he had loaned his car to Leng Samnang to drive home from a birthday party for Ranariddh at about 10.30 p.m. (1530 GMT) on Thursday.
Seven uniformed men, carrying AK-47s and dressed like the military or bodyguards, surrounded the editor, who was beaten and shot, he said.

Cheng Sokna noted the attack followed visits from representatives of the CPP and League of Cambodian Journalists, who he said tried unsucessfully to persuade his newspaper to change its anti-CPP stance.
But Chum Kanal, president of the league, denied the charges and condemned the shooting, adding, "I do not consider this a politically motivated attack".
